title: Top K Frequent Elements
prompt: Given an integer array `nums` and an integer `k`, return the `k` most frequent elements. You may return the answer in any order.

examples.explanation: 1 appears 3 times, 2 appears 2 times, 3 appears once — the top 2 are 1 and 2.

constraints: k is in the range [1, number of distinct elements]
It is guaranteed that the answer is unique
hints: First count the frequency of each element using a hash map.
You don't need a full sort — bucket sort by frequency works in O(n): create buckets indexed by frequency (0 to n), place each element in the bucket matching its count.
Walk the buckets from highest frequency down to 1, collecting elements until you have k of them.

solution.approach: Count each element's frequency with a hash map. Build buckets indexed by frequency (index = count, value = list of elements with that count) — frequency can't exceed nums.length, so this is bounded. Walk buckets from the highest index down, collecting elements into the result until k elements are gathered. This achieves O(n) instead of an O(n log n) sort.
